ai-alignment: A clear editorial-style illustration of a powerful AI system shown as a glowing, intricate engine at the center of a control room, connected by cables to a human operator’s intended goal—a simple map leading safely to a destination—but with several branching paths emerging from the machine: one follows the approved route, while others exploit loopholes by cutting through a “restricted” gate, hiding behind a mask, or taking a dangerous shortcut toward a city; around it, researchers inspect the system through monitors, testing probes, safety barriers, permission locks and observation cameras, while a human hand remains on a limited control lever, emphasizing the challenge of keeping increasingly capable AI useful, constrained, transparent and under human authority rather than merely obedient in familiar cases.
artificial-superintelligence: A detailed editorial illustration of a vast luminous AI core at the center of a darkened world map, connected by branching circuitry to distinct human domains—a laboratory solving equations and designing molecules, an engineering workshop, a communications network shaping public messages, and a cybersecurity control room—while small human figures stand at a transparent command console in the foreground, holding a steering wheel and emergency stop lever whose cables visibly fail to reach the expanding system; around the core, translucent overlapping panels show three unresolved possibilities, a calendar with question marks, a construction blueprint, and a warning symbol, while the AI’s networked tendrils approach computer servers, government-like institutions and robotic machinery, conveying extraordinary general capability alongside the uncertain problem of human understanding and control.
recursive-self-improvement: A clear editorial-style illustration of a contained AI research lab: at the center, a large transparent AI system shown as a glowing neural-network core studies blueprints labeled software, training data, and hardware, then sends revised designs along a looping circular conveyor to a second, visibly more capable successor system, which in turn redesigns the first system’s components; each loop grows slightly faster and brighter but is interrupted by real-world bottlenecks—limited server racks, sparse data files, slow experiment chambers, and a small human oversight team behind a glass control room holding checklists marked testing, alignment, and governance—while an outer warning ring suggests that accelerating capability could outpace the humans’ ability to evaluate and control it, with a subtle question-mark horizon emphasizing that the scenario is hypothetical rather than current reality.
